exposure: quality of care (childbirth satisfaction, early breastfeeding initiation, family-centered care, maternal satisfaction with postnatal care, breastfeeding support)
maternal factors (primiparity, antenatal breastfeeding plan, parenting self-efficacy)
cohort: A total of 160 mothers who had given birth within 12 weeks prior to the survey at a Finnish maternity hospital participated in the study.
finding: A lack of antenatal breastfeeding plan combined with lower parenting self-efficacy were the most significant predictors of non-exclusive breastfeeding.
